records.failureSummary: Implemented parseDuration in src/duration.mjs as a named export with a single text parameter, per FR-2 and technical specs T-1..T-9. Trust boundary: a typeof guard rejects every non-string input so nothing can throw; then the input is trimmed. A unit-less pure-integer branch returns the value as milliseconds. Otherwise one regex with alternation ms before h/m/s (longest-match, case-insensitive) scans integer+unit fragments; the gaps between fragments and the whole trimmed string must be whitespace-only and fully covered, else null. Conversion table h=3600000, m=60000, s=1000, ms=1; fragments are multiplied and summed to a number; duplicate-unit fragments return null. No third-party parser and no new build config. npm run build and npm run lint pass. npm test reports 34 of 35 subtests passing; the single failure is a contradictory assertion at test/duration.test.mjs:120 that asserts parseDuration(\"1ms10s30m1h\") === 5410500 while the spec-conformant sum is 1 + 10000 + 1800000 + 3600000 = 5410001. The sibling assertions on lines 118-119 use the 500ms fragment for that same 5410500 value, so line 120 is a test-data typo (1ms should be 500ms). No spec-conformant parser can satisfy line 120 without breaking lines 118-119. Because the harness scope is backend files only, neither the parser nor any test file was modified; the remaining work is a TEST task that corrects test/duration.test.mjs:120 so the suite can go green.
